title: Kibbeh
subtitle: Levantine spiced lamb and bulgur croquettes
excerpt: Oval croquettes made from a shell of fine bulgur wheat and minced lamb, filled with a spiced lamb and onion mixture with pine nuts and currants. Deep-fried until crisp and dark golden.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kibbeh is considered the national dish of Lebanon, Syria, and Jordan and is one of the most important dishes in the Arab world. There are dozens of regional varieties: baked kibbeh, raw kibbeh (kibbeh nayyeh, made from raw lamb and eaten like steak tartare), kibbeh in yoghurt sauce, fried kibbeh. The fried version is the one most widely encountered outside the Middle East. The shell is made from a paste of very fine bulgur wheat and raw lamb mixed to a smooth dough; the distinctive oval football shape (kibbeh means ball or oval in Arabic) takes practice to master but the taste is the same whatever the shape. The filling is a spiced lamb with onion, pine nuts, and dried fruit.

recipeTools.notes: Oil temperature for frying should be 175 C.

content.text: The bulgur must be soaked until fully softened, then squeezed very dry before mixing with the lamb. Any excess moisture in the dough will cause the kibbeh to burst during frying. The dough should feel pliable and smooth, not sticky. Keep your hands damp with cold water while shaping: this stops the mixture from sticking. The shell should be no thicker than 4 to 5 mm: too thick and the kibbeh is stodgy.

items.preparation: fine bulgur, soaked in cold water for 30 minutes, squeezed very dry
very finely grated, for the shell

content.text: Make the filling: heat the olive oil in a pan. Cook the diced onion for 8 minutes. Add the lamb mince and cook for 5 minutes until browned. Add the pine nuts, currants, allspice, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning. Cool completely.

Make the shell dough: combine the soaked, squeezed bulgur with the raw lamb mince, grated onion, allspice, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Mix very thoroughly, kneading for 3 to 4 minutes, until a smooth, cohesive dough forms. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.

With damp hands, take a portion of shell dough about the size of a golf ball. Flatten into an oval in your palm. Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre. Close the dough around the filling, shaping into a smooth oval or football shape. Seal the ends well. Repeat until all the dough and filling are used. You should get 16 to 18 kibbeh.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 175 C. Fry the kibbeh in batches of 4 to 5 for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep golden brown. Drain on kitchen paper. Serve hot with yoghurt dip and pitta bread.
